$description: The Publish workspace's home (studio.md §22.8): four sub-tabs over one body. Review changes is the change list grouped the way the site is organised (Pages, each content collection, Components, Layouts, Styles, Media, Other), each file's checkbox including it in the next publish (staging it), its Before and after opening the comparison (§21), then the checks, the destination, the summary and the one primary button. Deploys is the live site, any deploy running now with its steps, the history the host returns and the branch previews. Branches is the branch list with switch and create. Hosting is where the project is saved, where the site is hosted, the build adapter (an island: the Deploy section that moved here from Project Settings) and the address, with the deploy checklist under them. `publish/publish-workspace.ts` keeps every decision and hands this document strings and booleans; nothing here knows what a status letter means, which destination a host allows or what a deployment's stage is called.

style.$description: Fills the pane's stage by its own geometry, as the Media home does: the stage is `position: relative`, so the workspace takes the whole of it and scrolls its own body. The status colours are the theme's semantic tokens, so a check, a badge and a deployment's state follow light and dark without a hex anywhere.

& [part=\"review\"].$description: Two columns as the board draws them, the changes on the left and the publish card on the right; below 760px of pane the card drops under the list rather than squeezing it.

& [part=\"badge\"].$description: One letter and a colour, which is why the checkbox and the row's buttons carry the status in words as well.

& [part=\"check\"].$description: Centred, not baseline-aligned: the row can hold a small kit button, and a small kit control is layout-contained, so it has no baseline to align on.

& [part=\"check-icon\"], & [part=\"step-.$description: A kit icon for a check or a checklist link, sized by the kit's own property so it stays square; the activity feed's steps still draw a one-character glyph, which `minWidth` keeps on the same column.

& [part=\"checklist-step\"] > [part=\"st.$description: A baseline-aligned row places a kit icon's bottom edge on the text baseline, which draws it high; the negative end margin lowers it onto the line's middle.

& [part=\"destination-card\"] > [part=\".$description: A destination is a card with a name and a sentence saying what it does, inside one radio, as Add new's choice cards are: the reader hears one name and sees both lines.

& [part=\"failure\"].$description: `failure`, not `error`: a kit text field keeps a permanent live region named `error`, and a rule on that name would reach the summary field's (surface-part-names.test.ts).
